e-6174.knowledge_point: Determining a Rate of Change for a Given Function
e-6174.problem: A particle moves in a straight line. After $t$ seconds the particle is $\, f(t)=2t^3 - 5t + 9\,$ feet away from its initial position. What is the instantaneous rate of change of the particle's position as a function of $t?$
e-6174.worked_solution:
The instantaneous rate of change of the particle's position is equal to $f'(t).$ 

We take the derivative and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3}-5t+9) \\  & =6{t}^{2}-5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, after $t$ seconds, the instantaneous rate of change of the particle's position is $6t^2 - 5$ feet per second.

e-276.knowledge_point: Determining a Rate of Change for a Given Function at a Point
e-276.problem: Lizzie buys $b$ pounds of bananas at a price $p,$ in dollars, that can be modeled by the function $p(b)=5e^{-0.2b}.$ What is the instantaneous rate of change of the price when $b=5$ pounds?
e-276.worked_solution:
The instantaneous rate of change of the price when $b=5$ pounds is equal to $p'(5).$

First, we take the derivative and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{p}^{′}(b) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}b}(5{e}^{-0.2b}) \\  & =5{e}^{-0.2b}\cdot (-0.2) \\  & =-{e}^{-0.2b}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $b=5,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{p}^{′}(5) & =-{e}^{-0.2(5)} \\  & =-{e}^{-1} \\  & =-\frac{1}{e}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate change of the price when $b=5$ pounds is $-\dfrac{1}{e}$ dollars per pound.

e-275.knowledge_point: Further Determining Rates of Change in Geometrical Settings
e-275.problem:
A spherical balloon is being inflated so that its volume is increasing. Find the instantaneous rate at which the volume of the balloon is changing with respect to the radius at the moment when the diameter of the balloon is equal to $12\, \text{cm}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14037675/assets/e03fb046f74771676d7b1e83a1cf09176adcffaf8112e9de263404b8be74b026.png)
e-275.worked_solution:
Since we are given that the diameter of the balloon is $12\, \text{cm},$ its radius is $r =6\, \text{cm}.$ Now, we know that the volume of a sphere with radius $r$  is given by 

$$
V= V(r) = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3.
$$

Taking the derivative, the rate of change of $V(r)$  with respect to $r$ is 

$$
\eqalign{

V'(r) &= \dfrac{\textrm d }{\textrm d r}\left(  \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3\right)\[5pt]
 &  =  \dfrac{4}{3}\pi (3r^2)\[5pt]
 &= 4\pi r^2, 
}
$$

and evaluating at $r=6$ gives

$$
V'(6)=  4\pi (6)^2= 144\pi.
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate at which the volume of the balloon is changing when its diameter is $12\, \text{cm}\,$ is $\, 144\pi \, \text{cm}^3/\text{cm}.$

**Note:** We read $\text{cm}^3/\text{cm}$ as "centimeters cubed per centimeter".

The instantaneous rate of change of the spirit volume is equal to ${v}^{′}(t).$

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(8{e}^{t/2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot (8{e}^{t/2}) \\  & =4{e}^{t/2}.\end{aligned}

a
7101+e−t liters per day
b

355et liters per day
d
710et2+e−t liters per day

decision.explanation: By the chain rule, P'(t)=710e^t/(1+e^t)=710/(1+e^{-t}) liters per day, which matches option a.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem: The function $P(t)=710\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+{e}^{t})$ represents the volume of milk, in liters, produced on a farm $t$ days after the owner bought new cows. What is the instantaneous rate of change of the volume of produced milk as a function of $t?$
after.worked_solution:
The instantaneous rate of change of the volume of produced milk with respect to time is ${P}^{′}(t).$

Now, the rate of change of $P(t)$ with respect to $t$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(710\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+{e}^{t})) \\  & =710\,\frac{{e}^{t}}{1+{e}^{t}} \\  & =\frac{710}{1+{e}^{-t}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate of change of the volume of produced milk is  $\frac{710}{1+{e}^{-t}}$ liters per day.

after.worked_solution:
The instantaneous rate at which the distance traveled by the car is changing when $t=1$ second is equal to ${x}^{′}(1).$

Taking the derivative, the rate of change of $x(t)$ with respect to $t$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}+t)=2t+1,\end{aligned}
$$

and evaluating at $t=1$ gives

$$
{x}^{′}(1)=2(1)+1=3.
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate at which the distance traveled by the car is changing when $t=1$ second is $3$ meters per second.

The area $A$ of the circle above is increasing. The circumference and radius of the circle are $C$ and $r$ respectively. 
Find the rate of change of the area of the circle with respect to its circumference.
after.worked_solution:
The area of a circle is given by

$$
A=\pi {r}^{2},
$$

where $r$ is the radius of the circle.

We know that $C=2\pi r.$ so we can express the area $A$ as a function of the circumference $C$ by substituting $r=\frac{C}{2\pi }$ in the formula above. We get

$$
A=\pi {r}^{2}=\pi {(\frac{C}{2\pi })}^{2}=\frac{{C}^{2}}{4\pi }.
$$

Therefore, the rate of change of $A(C)$ with respect to $C$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{′}(C) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}C}(\frac{{C}^{2}}{4\pi }) \\  & =\frac{1}{4\pi }\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}C}({C}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4\pi }(2C) \\  & =\frac{C}{2\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the rate of change of the area of the circle with respect to its circumference.
content.worked_solution:
The area of a circle is given by

$$
A=\pi {r}^{2},
$$

where $r$ is the radius of the circle.

We know that $C=2\pi r.$ so we can express the area $A$ as a function of the circumference $C$ by substituting $r=\frac{C}{2\pi }$ in the formula above. We get

$$
A=\pi {r}^{2}=\pi {(\frac{C}{2\pi })}^{2}=\frac{{C}^{2}}{4\pi }.
$$

Therefore, the rate of change of $A(C)$ with respect to $C$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{′}(C) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}C}(\frac{{C}^{2}}{4\pi }) \\  & =\frac{1}{4\pi }\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}C}({C}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4\pi }(2C) \\  & =\frac{C}{2\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
We are given that $h=2s,$ so we can express the volume of the pyramid $V$ as a function of the base edge length $s$ by substituting $h=2s$ in the formula of the volume. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}V(s) & =\frac{1}{3}{s}^{2}h \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{s}^{2}(2s) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}{s}^{3}.\end{aligned}

Therefore, the rate of change of $V(s)$ with respect to $s$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}^{′}(s) & =\frac{d}{ds}\,(\frac{2}{3}{s}^{3}) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\cdot \frac{d}{ds}\,({s}^{3}) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\cdot 3{s}^{2} \\  & =2{s}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, the rate of change of the pyramid’s volume with respect to its base length $s$ is $2{s}^{2}.$

A spherical balloon is being inflated so that its volume is increasing. Find the instantaneous rate at which the volume of the balloon is changing with respect to the radius at the moment when the diameter of the balloon is equal to $20\,\text{cm}.$
after.worked_solution:
Since we are given that the diameter of the spherical balloon is $20\,\text{cm}$,  its radius $r$ is $10\,\text{cm}.$ Now, the volume of a sphere with radius $r$  is given by 

$$
V=V(r)=\frac{4}{3}\pi {r}^{3}.
$$

Taking the derivative, the rate of change of $V(r)$ with respect to $r$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}^{′}(r) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}r}(\frac{4}{3}\pi {r}^{3}) \\  & =\frac{4}{3}\pi (3{r}^{2}) \\  & =4\pi {r}^{2},\end{aligned}
$$

and evaluating at $r=10$ gives

$$
{V}^{′}(10)=4\pi (10)^{2}=400\pi .
$$

Therefore,  the instantaneous rate at which the volume of the balloon is increasing when the diameter is $20\,\text{cm}$ is $400\pi \,{\text{cm}}^{3}/\text{cm}.$

a
300cm3/cm
b
400πcm3/cm
c
1600πcm3/cm
d
400cm3/cm
e
300πcm3/cm
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since we are given that the diameter of the spherical balloon is 20cm, its radius r is 10cm. Now, the volume of a sphere with radius r is given by V=V(r)=43πr3.

Taking the derivative, the rate of change of V(r) with respect to r is

V′(r)=ddr(43πr3)=43π(3r2)=4πr2,

and evaluating at r=10 gives V′(10)=4π(10)2=400π.

Therefore, the instantaneous rate at which the volume of the balloon is increasing when the diameter is 20cm is 400πcm3/cm.
